options: Every read always returns the most recent write instantly
If no new writes occur, all replicas will converge to the same value over time
Data is never replicated across more than one node
Writes are rejected until every replica confirms them
questions.explain: Eventual consistency allows replicas to briefly disagree after a write, but guarantees convergence to the same value once writes stop.

questions.q: In the BASE acronym, what does "Basically Available" mean?
options: The system guarantees zero downtime under any circumstances
The system responds to requests most of the time, even during partial failures
The system is available only to a basic tier of paying customers
The system never accepts write requests
questions.explain: Basically Available means the system keeps responding through partial failures, prioritizing availability over the strict up-to-date guarantee of ACID consistency.

questions.q: What is a known risk of the last-write-wins conflict resolution strategy?
options: It requires every replica to be offline simultaneously
It can silently discard a legitimate update if clock timestamps aren't trustworthy
It never actually resolves any conflicts
It only works with strongly consistent systems
questions.explain: Last-write-wins relies on timestamps to pick a winner; if clocks are skewed or unreliable, a valid write can be discarded without warning.

questions.q: What makes a CRDT (Conflict-free Replicated Data Type) different from last-write-wins?
options: A CRDT is designed so concurrent updates merge automatically without losing information or needing a winner picked
A CRDT requires a single global lock before any write
A CRDT is only usable within one data center
A CRDT eliminates the need for replication entirely
questions.explain: CRDTs are data structures engineered so that concurrent, independent updates can always be merged into a consistent result without discarding data.

questions.q: Why is DNS a commonly cited real-world example of eventual consistency?
options: DNS records never change once published
Updated records propagate gradually as cached copies expire at their TTL, so different users may briefly see different values
DNS uses strong consistency to guarantee instant global updates
DNS has no caching mechanism at all
questions.explain: DNS deliberately trades instant global consistency for speed and availability: resolvers keep serving cached answers until the TTL expires, so propagation is gradual.
